tier_reason: The README 'Why QOIX?' table (PNG (stb) 89.73/14.34 mpps, QOI 201.9/150.8, QOIX 179.0/125.0, bits per pixel 10.29693/10.35162/7.93607) is first-party with no hardware, dataset, image count, compiler or flags. The in-repo harness examples/qoix/source/main.d exists, but in its current form it hard-codes the QOIX codec on images converted to 16-bit greyscale, never times PNG encoding, and ships an empty test-images folder, so it cannot regenerate the 8-bit colour table without edits; first-party numbers without methodology are C.

corrections.baseline: PNG via Gamut's own D translations of stb: stb_image 2.27 for PNG decode (source/gamut/codecs/stbdec.d) and stb_image_write 1.16 for PNG encode (source/gamut/codecs/stb_image_write.d), the README row 'PNG (stb)'. Not the C stb headers and not libpng. The README's 'QOI' row is Gamut's D translation of phoboslab/qoi (source/gamut/codecs/qoi.d).
corrections.workload: README 'Why QOIX?' table: mean decode and encode Mpixels/s and bits per pixel over unnamed '8-bit color images'; dataset, image count and machine not stated. The repo's harness examples/qoix/source/main.d (built by examples/qoix/eval.bat) times load and save of one codec per image from test-images/ (only a placeholder file is checked in) and averages mpps and bpp per image; as checked in it measures QOIX on 16-bit greyscale conversions, not 8-bit colour PNG/QOI/QOIX.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README 'Why QOIX?' table (decode mpps / encode mpps / bits per pixel): PNG (stb) 89.73 / 14.34 / 10.29693; QOI 201.9 / 150.8 / 10.35162; QOIX 179.0 / 125.0 / 7.93607. QOIX vs PNG (stb): 2.0x faster decode, 8.7x faster encode, 23 percent fewer bits per pixel (derived from page data). Gamut's QOI vs PNG (stb): 2.25x decode, 10.5x encode, about equal size (derived from page data). QOIX vs Gamut's QOI: 0.89x decode and 0.83x encode speed for 23 percent fewer bits per pixel (derived from page data). README text: 'QOIX and QOI generally outperforms PNG in decoding speed and encoding speed.'
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README table. The qoix harness's eval.bat runs 'dub -a aarch64 --combined -b release-nobounds -f' (DUB release build without bounds checks, aarch64 target), but the README does not say the table was produced with it.
corrections.license: BSL-1.0 (LICENSE file); dub.json declares 'BSL-1.0+MIT' and the QOI and QOIX codec sources (qoi.d, qoi2avg.d) carry MIT headers (Dominic Szablewski, wbd73, Guillaume Piolat); the 'boost+mit+bsd3' build configuration name implies a BSD-3 part (WebP). All OSI-approved.
corrections.caveats: First-party table with no hardware, dataset, image count, compiler or flags; the checked-in harness (examples/qoix/source/main.d) cannot regenerate it as written (QOIX only, greyscale 16-bit conversion, no PNG encode timing, empty test-images folder), and the convert tool's --time option (added 2026-07-21) times single files only. The baseline is a weak one: Gamut's D translations of stb_image / stb_image_write, whose PNG writer is documented upstream as unoptimized (20-50 percent larger files than a decent encoder), not libpng, libspng or fpng; the 10.3 bits per pixel PNG figure reflects that writer. The speed gain comes from switching format (QOI/QOIX are not PNG-compatible), and QOIX is explicitly 'not a storage format' whose bitstream may change between major Gamut tags. Lineage: Gamut's QOI codec is a D translation of the listed phoboslab/qoi, and QOIX is a D translation of wbd73's 'QOI2' modifications (nigeltao/qoi2-bikeshed issue 34) plus an LZ4 stage and Gamut's own greyscale and 10-bit plane codecs, so the distinct contribution is QOIX and the D library packaging. Low notability (52 stars).

notes: Numbers on the README are real and match the record; ratios check out. The 'QOI' half of this entry is a D port of listed phoboslab/qoi, so the orchestrator may want to frame the entry as QOIX (QOI2-derived plus LZ4) in a D image library; it is not a GitHub fork. Last commit 2026-07-21 confirmed, default branch main.

tier_reason: First-party numbers: bench/src/main.rs and the result files in benches/ are public, but the rustc version, flags and the exact Intel i9 model are not stated, and the README rows splice two different harnesses (the reference C qoibench.c for the 'qoi' row, the Rust bench for the 'rapid_qoi' row), so it is C. Tier unchanged from the record; verdict is downgrade because the headline 1.43x/1.52x decode claim is a cross-harness comparison and the only same-run comparison (benches/m1/rapid.md) shows rapid_qoi slower than the qoi crate at encoding.

corrections.baseline: Two different QOI implementations, both already listed, and neither the category baseline: the README 'qoi' row is the phoboslab/qoi reference C implementation run through its own qoibench.c with --nopng (benches/m1/reference.md and benches/intel-msvc/reference.md carry qoibench.c's exact output format, with the 'rate' column and 'Grand total' line), measured in a separate run from the rapid_qoi row; the repo's Rust harness bench/src/main.rs compares rapid_qoi against the qoi crate 0.4 (aldanor/qoi-rust). Not libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp or libavif.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README grand totals (ms, qoi vs rapid_qoi), where the 'qoi' row is the reference C qoibench run and the rapid_qoi row a separate Rust-harness run: Intel i9 decode 2.009 vs 1.404 and encode 2.706 vs 2.520; Apple M1 decode 1.676 vs 1.100 and encode 2.088 vs 1.836 (cross-harness ratios 1.43x/1.07x on i9 and 1.52x/1.14x on M1, derived from page data). The only same-run comparison, benches/m1/rapid.md (Rust harness, qoi crate vs rapid_qoi, 1 timed run): decode 1.161 vs 1.100 ms (rapid_qoi 1.06x faster) and encode 1.614 vs 1.836 ms (rapid_qoi 0.88x, about 14 percent slower), all derived from page data; rapid_qoi decodes faster in 12 of 13 image directories and encodes slower than the qoi crate in all 13. The README i9 rapid_qoi row (1.404/2.520 ms) is not in benches/intel-msvc/rapid.md, which reads 1.447/2.582 ms (1.39x decode, 1.05x encode vs the reference row, derived from page data). README text: 'one of the most efficient implementations of QOI encoder and decoder'.
corrections.workload: Whole-image in-memory QOI encode and decode of RGBA pixels from the qoi_benchmark_suite PNGs, averaged per image and totalled over the suite. Rust harness (bench/src/main.rs): images loaded with the image crate, input stream encoded by rapid_qoi, one untimed warm-up call then N timed runs per library (M1 file: 1 run; Intel file: 5 runs), results dropped without black_box. Reference rows: phoboslab qoibench.c --nopng, 5 runs. The M1 Rust run skipped 2 screenshot_game PNGs that the image crate could not decode (CRC error, bad keyword), so the README's M1 rows average slightly different image sets.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rapid_qoi rows: 'cargo run --release -p bench -- [iterations] [path]' (Rust release profile); rustc version and flags not stated; the Intel results folder is named benches/intel-msvc (Windows MSVC toolchain implied). Reference qoi rows: phoboslab qoibench.c; compiler and flags not stated (MSVC implied on Intel by the folder name, which would also handicap the C baseline against LLVM-built Rust).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 100 stars, 3 forks; crates.io 4,539,514 all-time downloads (201,344 recent), latest version 0.6.3
corrections.caveats: Off-baseline: compares only against other QOI implementations (phoboslab/qoi C reference and the qoi crate, both already listed), so it says nothing about libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp or libavif. Mixed result: the README's headline rows splice a reference qoibench.c run (5 runs) with a separate Rust-harness run (M1: 1 run), and the i9 rapid_qoi row matches no checked-in result file. In the same-run M1 file the qoi crate (aldanor/qoi-rust) encodes about 14 percent faster than rapid_qoi in aggregate and in every one of 13 directories, while rapid_qoi decodes about 6 percent faster; qoi-rust's own README says it was the fastest Rust QOI implementation 'by a noticeable margin'. The Intel i9 model, rustc version and C compiler for the reference rows are not stated. The benchmark numbers date from 2021-2022 and predate the 2026-01-16 'Apply bit hack optimisation from hardqoi' and follow-up correctness commit; the 2026-06-29 fix (clamp QOI_OP_RUN split, commit 1900bc3) only affects chunked decode_range calls that panicked, not the whole-image decode the benchmark times. Lineage: an independent safe-Rust (forbid(unsafe_code), no_std) implementation of the QOI format; it reproduces the qoi.h spec text in its docs but does not derive from qoi-rust, so it is not a wrapper or port.

notes: Keep as its own entry (independent Rust implementation, not a port of qoi-rust) with the mixed-result and off-baseline shortcomings recorded. The record misidentified the README 'qoi' row as the qoi crate; reference.md files are phoboslab qoibench.c output, so the README headline is rapid_qoi vs the C reference across two harnesses, while the same-run comparison against the listed qoi crate shows faster decode but slower encode.
